unmapped_findings: Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy of the alloy at LNT is 254 ± 6 J (RT 331 ± 4 J); this value belongs to the separate Charpy impact specimen (55 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm, V-notch depth 2 mm) rather than to the LNT tensile specimen.
Reduction of area of the alloy at LNT is 80 ± 1 % (RT 78 ± 0.5 %) from Table 2.

The LNT impact energy decreases about 30 % from 331 J (RT) to 254 J (LNT), attributed to the existence of 3.0 % α-phase in the austenite matrix; fine cracks form around voids generated by detachment of α (the γ/α interface serves as crack initiation site). Crack initiation energy Wm ≈ 80–100 J for both temperatures, propagation energy Wp drops from 251 J (RT) to 156 J (LNT).

Measured composition of the solution-treated specimen by wet-chemical analysis (wt.%): Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95, Fe Bal.; austenite (γ): Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86; ferrite (α): Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C '–', Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63.
Density of the investigated steel measured using the principle of Archimedes is 7.18 g·cm⁻³.

Based on electrolytic extraction, V is completely dissolved in the steel while Nb, Mo and W are partially dissolved, with approximately 0.047 wt.% Nb, 0.017 wt.% Mo and 0.024 wt.% W existing in MC carbide.

Deformation twinning nucleates at about 10 % tensile strain at LNT, whereas at RT it occurs at about 28 % tensile strain, indicating strong dependence of twinning on both deformation strain and temperature.
RT (sibling) values for context: YS 251 ± 3 MPa, UTS 580 ± 6 MPa, uniform elongation 38.5 ± 0.5 %, total elongation 52.0 ± 0.5 %, RT true stresses 339/483/635/723/800 MPa at 3/10/20/28/38 % strain.
